originality.rationale: The nearest full-text prior great-circle description specifies the 10-circle normal-cell geometry and the 20/60/12 face counts, but not the measured central-section type law or its exact spherical areas. The 2007 primary silhouette paper concerns asymptotic silhouette complexity of surface-approximating polyhedra, not this fixed-solid exact Haar law. The 2010 dodecahedral-slice extract concerns deterministic parallel cuts and volume, not random central orientations. The indexed central-icosahedron finding addresses a distinct polar solid/6-circle arrangement; polar duality does not equate central sections of the two solids. Exact probabilities are established by an independent complete chamber certificate and spherical excess. Historical priority remains provisional, especially for inaccessible 2010 full text.

value.rationale: The fully normalized polygon-type law for a random central slice of one of the five Platonic solids is a natural exact integral-geometric observable. Unlike a visual cell census, it requires the correct matching from normal chambers to cut-edge counts and exact spherical areas, and produces all probabilities without simulation or unproven asymptotics. The distinction between 6,8,10 section sides and 6,3,5 chamber sides is structurally informative and enables a complete benchmark for random plane slicing.
